title: Point-to-IfcGuid bind
description: A bind is a named identity claim: this layout point is that IFC entity, declared to a stated sigma in a stated frame at a stated epoch. It is not a measurement, not a harness digest, and not an authorization. Written down as a schema because until it was, every MCP client invented its own shape -- and the fold accepted three fields as a bind.

claim_scope.description: A bind claims record integrity and nothing else. It is not field evidence and does not make a quantity traceable.

global_id.description: An IFC GlobalId. The `not` pattern below is LINT, not the identity law: it catches the display names this project's demos use (Opening-1, Beam-B1) because pasting one in is the common mistake, and it catches nothing else -- RoomA passes, a truncated Guid passes, a Guid from another file passes. Identity is established by assert_bind_in_world (the Guid, with that class, is in the compiled world) together with the ifc_class enum. A bind that satisfies this pattern has been spell-checked; a bind that satisfies assert_bind_in_world names something that exists.

ifc_class.description: Bindable classes only. Widening this list is a claim that the lowerer carries that class, so it is a code change, not a file edit.

digest.description: Canonical digest over payload. When present it must match; a declared digest that does not match its own payload is refused rather than recomputed.

payload.description: The bound claim. sigma is required: a bind that does not say how well the point is known cannot be used to license an observation, and 'the CAD said so' is a sigma with a reason, not an absence of one.

frame_id.description: Which coordinate frame the point is in. Two frames are not one frame because both are called 'site'.

epoch.description: When the bind was established. 'design-declared' is a legitimate epoch and is not a field resection.

sigma.description: Positive and finite. Zero would claim an exact point, which no layout process delivers.

sigma_reason.description: Where sigma came from, in prose a surveyor would accept. A number with no reason is not a budget.

space_id.description: The IfcSpace this point sits in, as space:ifc:<GlobalId>. Optional, and it is the field the inspectability fold reads to place a bind in a space.

quantity.description: Optional. The quantity a later observation would touch, so the bind says which slot it licenses rather than leaving a client to guess. Naming it does not observe it.

receipt_digest.description: Optional. Links this bind to an evidence receipt. A full 64-character sha256, the same width as every other digest here -- short prefixes appear only in test fixtures and are not a reason to widen a schema, because a reader should never have to guess whether a 16-character string is a whole digest or the front of one. It does NOT close the fold's evidence.as_built hole: identity and evidence are two holes, and a bind that cites a receipt is still only an identity claim.

world_digest.description: Optional. Which lowering the Guid was checked against. Local to a machine and a path spelling: see docs/digest-portability-v1.md. A bind that records it can be re-checked offline; one that does not must be re-checked against a live world.

payload.additionalProperties_note: Open on purpose: a bind file carries prose a closed schema would reject -- a note, an omitted_on_purpose block, a surveyor's name. Open also means an agent can write authorized: true or traceable: true. gat.harness.point_bind refuses those by name, anywhere in the document, via FORBIDDEN_KEYS, and refuses a second claim_scope nested under payload. They are refused rather than dropped, because a silently dropped claim leaves whoever wrote it believing the bind carried it. Unknown keys that are not authority claims are kept out of the digest and dropped by PointBind.to_document().

not_claimed: a bind is not field evidence
a bind does not condition belief or shrink Sigma
a gat.harness --commit digest is not a bind
a JSON object that only says schema: cse-point-bind-v1 is not a bind
a paragraph from an MCP agent is not a bind
the global_id pattern is lint; assert_bind_in_world is the identity check

digest_note: The digest covers point_id, ifc_class, global_id, name, space_id, frame_id, epoch, sigma, sigma_unit, sigma_reason, quantity, receipt_digest and world_digest. quantity is inside it because a bind licensing Width is a different claim from one licensing Height, so two binds identical but for quantity must not share an identity.
